system.name: DPA-Store
system.one_liner: a NIC-resident ordered key-value store that answers requests on-path using a learned index, while the host asynchronously applies structural updates

components.name: BF3 packet processing
components.role: receives incoming request packets on the NIC

components.name: DPA traverser threads
components.role: on-path DPA threads that are assigned incoming requests and walk the NIC-side learned index to fetch values or buffer inserts

components.name: Inner_0 (root)
components.role: root node of the learned-index tree, mirrored on both the NIC and host sides

components.name: Inner
components.role: internal learned-index node guiding traversal toward a leaf

components.name: Leaf
components.role: leaf node holding a leaf-level model, key ranges/values and an insert buffer

components.name: Hot-pair cache
components.role: thread-local cache for hot key-value pairs

components.name: insert buffer
components.role: per-leaf buffer that batches inserts/updates before propagating them to the host

components.name: new Inner
components.role: newly created internal node produced by a host-side structural update

components.name: new Leaf
components.role: newly created leaf node produced by a host-side structural update, e.g. from a leaf split

components.name: 'stitch' packages
components.role: packaged structural updates sent from the host back to the NIC

components.name: 'patch' requests
components.role: requests sent from the NIC to the host asking it to perform a structural update, e.g. when an insert buffer is full

components.name: Allocators
components.role: host-side allocators tracking DRAM space and DPA space for new nodes

flows.what: request packets assigned to a DPA traverser thread
walks the NIC-side learned index from the root
value fetched per DMA using the leaf-level model
inserts placed in the leaf-level insert buffer
a patch request is added when the insert buffer becomes full
host 'patch' threads update the host tree, creating new nodes
structural updates packaged for the NIC
DPA 'stitch' threads apply host updates back into the NIC-side tree

content.key_idea: DPA-Store keeps a mirrored learned-index tree on the NIC (answering reads/inserts on-path) and on the host, exchanging lightweight 'patch' requests and 'stitch' packages across the PCIe boundary to keep them in sync without blocking the NIC-side fast path.
content.reading_order: Left to right across the NIC-host PCIe boundary: packets enter on the NIC side (I), traverse the tree (II-IV), and patch/stitch messages synchronize with the host-side tree (V) shown on the right.

palette.used_for: dark green text/icon for the DPA traverser threads and the step markers on the NIC side
pale blue fill for Inner/root tree nodes
gray fill for Leaf node icons
pale orange background for the Host-side region and 'patch'-related labels
cyan fill for the NIC-side background region

style.font: mixed serif/monospace (Times New Roman and Courier New), roughly 5.5-11pt, bold for headers
style.arrows: very many thin lines forming the tree edges, plus a handful of curved cross-boundary arrows for patch/stitch traffic
style.icons: vector icons for metadata, key-child/value pairs, insert buffers and ring queues, explained in a small legend

encoding.color_means: cyan region = NIC DRAM (on-path learned index), orange region = Host DRAM (host-side tree and allocators), green = DPA traverser/patch step labels and new nodes created by a structural update
encoding.line_style_means: solid black edges draw the learned-index tree on each side; colored curved arrows carry 'patch request' and 'stitch package' traffic across the NIC-host PCIe boundary
encoding.emphasis: a dashed vertical line separating NIC-side and Host-side, with green-highlighted 'new Inner'/'new Leaf' nodes, calls out that structural updates originate on the host and are later stitched back into the NIC-resident index
reusable_patterns: mirrored tree structure on both sides of a NIC/host PCIe boundary, with lightweight patch/stitch messages keeping them in sync
small icon legend explaining tree-node glyphs
weaknesses: identically named Inner/Leaf/Inner_0(root) nodes appear on both the NIC and host sides, which requires reading the side/background color to disambiguate

evidence: Request packets are assigned on-path to a DPA traverser thread
Values are fetched per DMA using leaf-level models

summary: DPA-Store is an ordered key-value store that runs entirely on a BlueField-3 SmartNIC's on-path DPA cores, answering requests without host involvement on the common path. The figure splits into a cyan NIC-side and an orange Host-side across a dashed PCIe boundary, each holding a mirrored learned-index tree of Inner nodes and Leaf nodes. On the NIC, incoming request packets are assigned to a DPA traverser thread (I), which walks the tree from the root (II), fetches values per DMA using leaf-level models (III), and places inserts into a leaf's insert buffer (IV); a full insert buffer triggers a patch request to the host. The host's patch threads then perform structural updates, creating new Inner/Leaf nodes (V) that are packaged and stitched back into the NIC-side tree by DPA stitch threads.
summary_zh: DPA-Store是运行于BlueField-3网卡DPA核心的有序键值存储:PCIe两侧各维护镜像索引树,NIC侧遍历线程查找/取值/插入(I-IV),缓冲满时向主机发patch,主机更新树(V)后stitch回NIC。
